# Implement the Nibfin semantic Light/Dark design tokens

> **Proposed raw Scope for a NORMAL post-Bootstrap Nibfin Issue.** This is a review draft, not an existing GitHub Issue, an approved Shape, or proof of execution.

**Owner:** `taco3064/nibfin-core`  
**Planning ID:** `DOC02` (not a GitHub Issue number)  
**Product authority:** [Nibfin Proposal draft 0.9, current §14 and related clauses](https://app.notion.com/p/40006b644a2080dab1a8c2e562f95373); specific anchors: §14.2–14.4  
**Mode:** Normal Scope → independent Shape → Deliver → Accept → CI/Review → authorized Merge/Closure.  
**Website placement and host (Owner-confirmed for this Scope Plan):** public site source `nibfin-core/website/` with **GitHub Pages deployed by GitHub Actions**. This attributable Owner/Scope decision specifies the route left open under Proposal §14; it does not announce a deployed site, confer GitHub write privileges or create a fourth product Repository.

## Planned GitHub label metadata and safe activation

This is a **proposed raw Scope**, not a currently published or executable GitHub Issue. The **planned active-state GitHub labels are exactly `scope`**; never pre-apply `shaped` or `delivered` at Scope Publish. The planned publication sequence is:

1. After the Phase 0 / C18 cutover and **separate approval of the exact full manifest**, create this raw Issue with **no Nibfin lifecycle labels**. GitHub `issues.opened` is only a wake-up; without `scope` and an actual authorization grant it must not start Shape/Deliver.
2. Resolve every real predecessor to its stable GitHub Issue ID, create the **native `Blocked by` relationships**, then independently read back both sides. If this Issue has no predecessors, explicitly verify that its approved native predecessor set is empty; never synthesize a dependency on a manually closed Bootstrap #1 or on the C18 report.
3. Re-read the raw Issue Body, actual labels, assignees, dependency graph, current repository state, authentic execution identity and authorized runtime policy. Confirm the approved Scope enrollment / Runner conditions and **any separate execution authorization**. Unavailable or ambiguous evidence leaves the Issue **open without `scope`**, not silently eligible.
4. Only after the dependency and authorization preflight, an **authorized publisher** adds `scope`, reads back the exact GitHub label set and logs the real provider result. A `scope` label is observable workflow state **but not a grant**. The resulting Issue can be considered for Shape only when the trusted Core additionally authorizes the work.
5. The subsequent trusted lifecycle may apply `shaped` only following independent Shape validation, authorized Body/metadata publication and exact read-back. `delivered` and closure require the actual independent Accept, CI/Review, authorized Merge and closure proofs. Neither label may be fabricated by Scope Plan/Publish.

Creation labels: **`[]`** · Authorized Scope activation delta: **`+scope`** · Planned post-activation set: **`[scope]`** · Never at raw publication: **`shaped`, `delivered`**. These are *planning metadata*, not current GitHub labels.

## Scope activation wake-up path and verification (native GitHub, no extra scheduler)

At each **authorized** future `scope` activation, determine **which actual actor/credential** writes the label and **which workflow event** can start the installed Nibfin entry. A trusted publisher adding `scope` via an ordinary **workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN`** must **not** rely on the resulting `issues.labeled` event creating another Actions run: GitHub suppresses most workflow-triggered recursion. Where this is the actual actor, the approved implementation must use the **existing legitimate `workflow_dispatch` or `repository_dispatch` route** (or a separately evidenced authorized non-`GITHUB_TOKEN` event actor), with bounded Issue identity and current authorization. The receiving Core must re-read live Issue Body, native dependencies, labels, assignees, grant and execution version before admission; neither label nor payload grants execution.

Do not fire duplicate wake-ups via both native event and dispatch for the same intended activation. Read back the actual label mutation and the Actions Run/attempt or deny/pending result; an accepted API request alone does not prove a Job started. If no authenticated allowed wake-up path is available, leave the Issue **not eligible to run**, reconcile unknown effects and block that activation. This is an integration contract for existing GitHub/Core capabilities, not a new event relay or scheduler.


## Goal

Establish one verified semantic token source and accessible Nibfin visual direction across Starlight documentation and Astro pages.

## Included

- Define Light and Dark semantic tokens for background, surfaces, body/secondary text, borders, links, focus, interactive accent, status, and code blocks in one maintainable stylesheet/source.
- Map those tokens into Starlight properties and Tailwind CSS theme semantics so future shadcn/ui and React consumers reference the same tokens.
- Adopt DM Sans for text and Space Grotesk for heading hierarchy; express the approved Midnight Indigo + Soft Violet direction without copying Shoal’s green accent.
- Apply the design to real Starlight navigation, search, sidebar, table of contents, articles and code blocks (not only a landing hero).
- Exercise both themes, keyboard focus, text/code contrast and narrow-screen styles with deterministic screenshots/contrast checks where available.

## Out of Scope

- Inventing a second token store in React components or Tailwind, locking in unapproved exact swatch hex values, or copying any Shoal page layout.
- Production website release, marketing/homepage content, or adding a separate component library.

## Selected engineering route (nonbinding)

Use Starlight `customCss` and `--sl-*` variable overrides plus one shared semantic theme file for Tailwind and shadcn consumer mappings. Treat the Proposal’s four prior hex values as candidates, not normative tokens.

## Proposed native Blocked by

- **`DOC01`**, `nibfin-core`: Astro/Starlight workspace is required before theme/content integration.

These are *planning identities* only; at authorized Publish time resolve exact GitHub Issue URLs and independently read back the native relationships. A Markdown line, closed manual #1, or cutover marker is not a protected work grant.


## Own completion and preliminary observable checks

Both theme variants render legibly in local Starlight docs, including mobile navigation, active/focus states, search and code blocks; token consumers resolve to the same source with no duplicated brand palette.

The eventual formal Shape may define more precise reproducible positive/negative acceptance tests **within this same approved raw Scope**. It cannot silently add other work or claim later real E2E as a local implementation pass.

## Produced interface or evidence handoff

Stable public-safe light/dark semantic CSS and font specification consumed by DOC03 and DOC04.

## Later verifier and downstream consumer

DOC03 consumes the exact token names; DOC04 uses them in homepage UI; DOC08 checks real published themes on mobile and keyboard.

## Public trust and release constraints

- Published docs, site metadata, workflows and demo snippets must not reveal private Kairo source, secrets, privileged runner paths, owner credentials or protected operational evidence.
- `scope`, `shaped`, `delivered`, a deployment acknowledgement, or a screenshot cannot independently prove Core authorization, release success or full product support.
- The public site has no GitHub Issue/Runner/CI/Merge control authority, login product, SaaS backend or separate policy/data store.
- Protect public Pages publication from untrusted fork PRs. Unknown external deployment or required artifact state remains unknown until authenticated read-back.
- Starlight/Doc routes are a documentation projection, not a second product specification SSOT. Any product behavior contradiction must be resolved in authoritative Proposal, not by editing marketing copy.

## Estimate and planning limitations

250–600 meaningful maintained LOC (medium confidence; keep tokens centralized).  
Selected paths, dependency versions, website hosting permissions, future repository checks and available release identities must be verified during Shape/Publish; no source changes, CI, page deployment, or real validation have been performed for this draft.

## Provider references consulted for this planning route

- https://starlight.astro.build/guides/customization/

## Approved website route and actual publication readiness

The Owner has explicitly selected **`nibfin-core/website/` + GitHub Pages, deployed via GitHub Actions** for this planning slice, consistent with Proposal §14's Scope-level host-selection boundary. This is a **resolved route choice**, not an outstanding Docs architecture question. The Issue nevertheless remains a raw Scope **candidate**, requiring post-C18 actual-work deduplication, independent Owner approval of the final issue/dependency manifest, authorized Scope Publish, trusted Shape and the applicable CI/Release/read-back gates. A site build or mock is not proof of live publication.

## Phase 0 → Phase 1 entry (not a native dependency)

This is a **post-cutover candidate**, not eligible for Scope Publish until the independent external C18 cutover report confirms an actual authorized Public Repository E2E, and all three newly initialized repositories have proven installed Core/Action/CLI and legitimate Runner/Workflow settings. Phase 0 manual #1 closure is **not** protected `delivered`; neither C18 nor #1 is added here as a native predecessor. The formal issue creator must refresh current sources, detect already-completed work, obtain owner approval and publish only outstanding work with trusted native edges.
